I'm **Iván Alonso**, a geographer and remote sensing specialist based near Erlangen (MSc Environmental & Climate Sciences, FAU).

I built this atlas to show how open Earth observation data can turn climate risks into clear, local evidence for planners, forest managers and municipalities.

## What this project demonstrates

| Area | Tools and methods |
|---|---|
| Earth observation | Sentinel-2 L2A, cloud masking (SCL), spectral indices (NDVI, NDMI), multi-year composites and anomalies |
| Cloud processing | Google Earth Engine (Python API) |
| Geospatial Python | rasterio, geopandas, numpy/pandas, folium; raster–vector integration on a common grid |
| Spatial analysis | Multi-criteria susceptibility index, distance-decay factors, sensitivity analysis |
| Open data | ESA WorldCover, DLR Tree Species Germany, OpenStreetMap, WDPA, SRTM |
| Communication | Reproducible notebooks, interactive web maps, Quarto website, English + German summaries |

## Approach

Every case study follows the same structure: **problem → data → method → results → recommendation → limitations**. Assumptions are stated explicitly and tested where possible. Limitations are part of the result, not a footnote.
